payload.summary: All four amendments have solid technical merit. Three address concrete correctness or regression-coverage gaps in chemistry/snapshot handling, and the fourth removes a real metadata drift hazard by consolidating duplicated domain definitions.

votes.rationale: `compute_o2_kla` assumes `REFERENCE_SA_V_CM2_PER_L` matches the default `TankState` geometry/substrate setup, but nothing currently enforces that calibration link. If the default dimensions, fill model, or substrate displacement change, default-tank gas exchange silently shifts. A direct regression test is low-cost and appropriately guards that invariant.

`normalize_snapshot_object` only backfills canonical chemistry keys; it does not remove API-added metadata fields before `serde_json::from_value`. Parsing works today only because `TankSnapshot` accepts unknown fields by default. Existing tests cover legacy aliases but not the actual enriched API payload shape, so an end-to-end deserialization test is justified and would catch future regressions.

This is a real consistency bug. `TankSnapshot::from_state()` freshly solves carbonate equilibrium for pH/CO2, but TDS and conductivity still read through `WaterState::bicarbonate_mg_total`, which is explicitly documented as a stale-able cache until `resolve_carbonate_state()` runs. That can produce snapshots with self-inconsistent chemistry, so deriving the bicarbonate contribution from the fresh solve or forcing a refresh is the correct fix.

The 7-ion TDS scope is domain metadata, yet it is duplicated across `tank_core`, `tank_api`, and `tank_tui`. That creates an avoidable drift risk between the actual calculation and the explanatory surfaces. Centralizing the authoritative ion-set/scope definition in `tank_core` improves maintainability and robustness while still allowing API and TUI to format it as needed.
